classification.difficultyReason: Prove equality by accounting for overlap when adding two semicircle areas.

content.prompt: Two semicircles are drawn in a quarter circle, as shown in the diagram below. Show that the areas $A_1$ and $A_2$ indicated in the diagram are equal.

spec.description: Quarter circle with inward semicircles on its vertical and horizontal radii. All three arcs and labels A₁ and A₂ are retained. White identifies the uncovered region A₂; light blue identifies semicircles and solid blue their overlap.
spec.mathematics: Quarter circle centred at (0,0), radius 2. Semicircles have centres (0,1) and (1,0), radius 1, and intersect at (0,0) and (1,1).
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied regions and labels are shown; no answer measurements are added.

answer.short:
$A_1=A_2$.

The two semicircle areas together equal the quarter-circle area; their overlap balances the uncovered region.
answer.worked:
Let each semicircle have radius $r$. The quarter circle has radius $2r$.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{two semicircles}}&=2\left(\frac12\pi r^2\right)\\A_{\text{two semicircles}}&=\pi r^2\\A_{\text{quarter circle}}&=\frac14\pi(2r)^2\\A_{\text{quarter circle}}&=\pi r^2\end{align*}$$
Let $B$ be the area covered by exactly one semicircle. Adding the semicircle areas counts the overlap twice, whereas the quarter circle contains the overlap once and also contains $A_2$.
$$\begin{align*}B+2A_1&=B+A_1+A_2\\A_1&=A_2\end{align*}$$
